$comment: TempHire's validation rules, for the client and the server: ValidationController serves them to the client, which installs them into Breeze, and the server checks them on every save (TempHirePersistenceManager).

The global breeze validator brings the entities' data annotations ([Required], [MaxLength], ...) into the framework.  On the client it runs Breeze's validators, which Breeze builds from those annotations; on the server it runs the annotations themselves (AddDataAnnotations("breeze") in Program.cs).  The other rules are the ones annotations cannot express.

Property names are the client's (camelCase), because the expressions run in the browser too; the server matches them to its properties case-insensitively.  There are no display names: on the server a message names the property as the payload does, and the client takes its display names from Breeze.
Address.stateId: the foreign key is a non-nullable Guid, so an address without a state has the empty Guid, which [Required] accepts.

Addresses are U.S. addresses: a state, and a U.S. ZIP code.  Phone numbers are U.S. numbers in one field, area code included, in any of the common ways to write one: 10 digits; with dashes, dots or spaces between area code, prefix and line number, the same separator throughout; or the area code in parentheses, (206) 555-1234 or (206)555-1234.  Any of these may start with the country code, 1 or +1.  The clients rewrite a valid number as (206) 555-1234 when the user leaves the field.  The pattern has no backreferences: it runs in JavaScript and .NET, which treat a reference to a group that didn't match differently.
A date of birth is a plausible one: not in the future, and not further back than the longest documented human life, 122 years and 164 days, so no more than 123 years ago.

context.messageTemplate: A staffing resource must have at least one address
A staffing resource must have at least one phone number
A staffing resource must be at least 18 years old when hired
'%displayName%' can't be in the future or more than 123 years ago
'%displayName%' must be a U.S. ZIP code, like 98101 or 98101-1234
'%displayName%' must be a U.S. phone number, like (206) 555-1234
